name: Florentino Pérez
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Pérez began his professional career in 1971 at age 24 in a minor administrative role at the Madrid city council; his major business achievements (buying bankrupt construction company Padrós in 1983 at age 36, becoming Real Madrid president in 2000 at age 53) all came well after 26.
early_history_summary: Pérez studied civil engineering at the Polytechnic University of Madrid and began his career in the early 1970s in government roles at the Madrid city council and Ministry of Public Works. He flirted with politics as secretary-general of the Democratic Reformist Party (1979–1986) before entering business in his mid-30s.
evidence_summary: No material milestone by age 26 was identified. Pérez's career began with government administrative roles in his early twenties, followed by an unsuccessful foray into politics in his late twenties and early thirties. His business empire began only at age 36 when he purchased the bankrupt Padrós construction company in 1983.

name: Mikhail Khodorkovsky
milestone_by_age_26: Founded Bank Menatep in 1989 at age 26, one of the first privately owned commercial banks in Russia, after establishing a successful import-export business and the Youth Centre for Scientific and Technical Development in 1987 at age 24.
early_history_summary: Khodorkovsky graduated from the Mendeleev Institute of Chemical Technology in 1986 and became deputy head of the Komsomol at his university. Leveraging Komsomol connections during perestroika, he founded the Youth Centre for Scientific and Technical Development in 1987, expanded into computer import-export, and acquired a banking license in 1989 to form Bank Menatep.
family_context_summary: Both parents were chemical engineers at a factory making measuring instruments in Moscow. They were middle-class, well-educated Soviets who silently opposed communism but kept this from their son.
parent_family_domain_summary: Parents were chemical engineers but had no business or financial domain expertise to transfer. Khodorkovsky followed their path initially by studying chemical engineering before pivoting to business.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Komsomol network, perestroika timing, Moscow frontier, university pipeline
evidence_summary: Khodorkovsky leveraged his position as deputy head of the Komsomol at the Mendeleev Institute to access the nascent private enterprise opportunities created by Gorbachev's perestroika reforms. In 1987 at age 24, he founded the Youth Centre for Scientific and Technical Development, which provided market research and technology brokering. By 1989 at age 26, he had acquired a banking license and formed Bank Menatep, one of Russia's first private commercial banks, with several business partners including Leonid Nevzlin. His parents were factory engineers with no business background; his advantage came from institutional positioning within the Komsomol during a unique historical window.

name: Keke Rosberg
milestone_by_age_26: Won the German Formula Super Vee Championship in 1975 at age 26, winning ten of the 21 races he entered that season, after becoming Scandinavian and European kart champion in 1973.
early_history_summary: Rosberg started karting as a toddler in Finland, became Finnish kart champion five times, and won the Scandinavian and European kart championship in 1973 at age 25. He progressed through Formula Vee and Super Vee, winning the German Championship in 1975, before moving to European Formula Two and eventually making his F1 debut in 1978 at age 29.
family_context_summary: Father was a veterinarian and mother a chemist; both competed in rallies. The family moved from Sweden to Finland when Rosberg was young. There was no silver spoon — Rosberg had to wheel, deal, and hustle to finance his early career.
parent_family_domain_summary: Both parents competed in rallies, providing early exposure to motorsport culture. However, there is no evidence they provided professional racing connections or financial backing for a career in racing.
primary_early_advantage_tags: karting from childhood, parental rally exposure, Fred Opert patronage, self-financed hustle
evidence_summary: Rosberg started karting as a toddler and became an accomplished kart racer by his teens, winning five Finnish kart championships and the Scandinavian and European championship in 1973. His parents were rally competitors, giving him early motorsport exposure, but there was no silver spoon — he never spent his own money on racing and hustled to find sponsors and patrons. American entrant Fred Opert became a key patron, providing cars for Formula Two, Atlantic, and Pacific campaigns. In 1975 at age 26, he won the German Formula Super Vee Championship with ten wins from 21 races, a material milestone in a recognized international racing series.

name: Andre Geim

His groundbreaking graphene work came in 2004 at age 46, and the Nobel Prize in 2010 at age 52.

parent_family_domain_summary: Parents were engineers, providing a technically oriented family environment, but there is no evidence of direct domain advantage in condensed matter physics or graphene research.
evidence_summary: No material milestone by age 26 was identified. Geim was a PhD student at the Institute of Solid State Physics in Chernogolovka during his mid-twenties, working on helicon resonance in metals — a subject he later described as dead. His PhD was completed in 1987 at age 29, and his Nobel Prize-winning graphene work came in 2004 at age 46. His early research papers were cited only twice by co-authors.

name: Ian Gillan
milestone_by_age_26: Joined Deep Purple in 1969 at age 24 and recorded the landmark album 'Deep Purple in Rock' in 1970 at age 25, which set new standards for hard rock vocals and launched the band to international fame.
early_history_summary: Gillan was influenced by Elvis Presley from a young age and started fronting local bands as a teenager in the early 1960s. He joined The Javelins in 1962 at age 17, then Wainwright's Gentlemen, before being recruited to Episode Six in 1965. After four years of relentless gigging with Episode Six, drummer Mick Underwood connected him to Ritchie Blackmore, and Gillan joined Deep Purple in 1969.
family_context_summary: Father Bill was a storekeeper at a London factory who left school at 13. Mother Audrey came from a musical family — her father was an opera singer and amateur pianist. The family was working-class in Hounslow, Middlesex.
parent_family_domain_summary: Mother's family enjoyed music and singing, and her father was an opera singer, providing a musical environment. However, there is no evidence of professional music industry connections or formal training.
primary_early_advantage_tags: working-class background, musical grandfather, years of gigging, Roger Glover partnership, British rock wave
evidence_summary: Gillan started performing in bands at age 17 with The Javelins, then spent four years gigging relentlessly with Episode Six from 1965 to 1969, sometimes playing five shows a night. This apprenticeship built his vocal power and stage presence. His mother's father was an opera singer, providing a musical heritage, but the family was working-class with no industry connections. The British rock explosion of the late 1960s created a structural wave, and his recruitment to Deep Purple in 1969 at age 24 — alongside bassist Roger Glover, his Episode Six bandmate — gave him the platform to record 'Deep Purple in Rock' (1970), a landmark hard rock album, by age 25.

name: Richard Gere
milestone_by_age_26: Took the lead role in the original London stage production of 'Grease' in 1973 at age 24, after making his Broadway debut in 1971 at age 22 and performing with the Seattle Repertory Theatre and Provincetown Playhouse.
early_history_summary: Gere attended the University of Massachusetts on a gymnastics scholarship but dropped out to pursue acting. He worked at the Seattle Repertory Theatre and Provincetown Playhouse in 1969, made his Broadway debut in the rock opera 'Soon' in 1971, understudied the lead in Broadway's 'Grease' in 1972, and took the lead in the London production of 'Grease' in 1973. He made his film debut in 1975 at age 26.
family_context_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources beyond general biographical information. Gere attended college on a gymnastics scholarship, suggesting a middle-class background.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Broadway pipeline, West End lead, gymnastics scholarship, Seattle Repertory Theatre, New York theater scene
evidence_summary: Gere dropped out of college to pursue acting and quickly ascended the theater pipeline: Seattle Repertory Theatre and Provincetown Playhouse in 1969, Broadway debut in 1971, and the lead in the London production of 'Grease' in 1973 at age 24. His gymnastics background gave him physical presence. By age 26, he had also made his film debut in 'Report to the Commissioner' (1975). However, his major fame came later with 'American Gigolo' (1980) at age 31. Family background is not well-documented in reviewed sources.

name: Mario Kempes
milestone_by_age_26: Won the 1978 FIFA World Cup with Argentina at age 24, finishing as the tournament's top scorer (6 goals) and best player (Golden Ball), after becoming top scorer in the Argentine championship at age 20 and La Liga top scorer at age 22-23.
early_history_summary: Kempes grew up in Bell Ville, Córdoba — known as Argentina's 'national capital of football' — and began playing at age 7. He joined the Talleres reserves at 14 and debuted professionally for Instituto in 1973 at age 19, scoring 11 goals in 13 games. He moved to Rosario Central where he scored 85 goals in 105 matches, then transferred to Valencia in 1976, where he became La Liga's top scorer twice.
family_context_summary: Father was of German heritage and mother was Italian. Both parents' professions are not documented in reviewed sources. Kempes grew up in Bell Ville, a small town known for manufacturing footballs.
parent_family_domain_summary: No evidence of family football background or professional sports connections. The town's football culture may have provided informal exposure.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Bell Ville football culture, Instituto youth academy, early professional debut, Ardiles peer, Argentine football pipeline
evidence_summary: Kempes grew up in Bell Ville, a town famously known as Argentina's 'national capital of football' for its ball manufacturing industry. He started playing at age 7, joined the Talleres reserves at 14, and debuted professionally for Instituto at 19 alongside Ossie Ardiles. His prolific goalscoring — 11 goals in 13 games for Instituto, 85 in 105 for Rosario Central — earned him a transfer to Valencia in 1976 at age 22, where he became La Liga's top scorer twice. By age 24, he won the 1978 World Cup as top scorer and best player. No family football background or financial advantage is documented; his advantage came from early immersion in Argentine football culture and the youth-to-professional pipeline.

name: Cat Stevens
milestone_by_age_26: Scored a UK #2 hit single with 'Matthew and Son' in 1966 at age 18, followed by a debut album of the same name in 1967, establishing him as a major British pop star while still a teenager.
early_history_summary: Born Steven Demetre Georgiou in London to a Greek Cypriot father and Swedish mother who ran a restaurant, Stevens became interested in music through the family's baby grand piano. At 15, inspired by the Beatles, he persuaded his father to buy him a guitar. He got his first publishing deal at 17 in 1965, was discovered by producer Mike Hurst, signed to Decca/Deram, and released 'I Love My Dog' (UK #28) and 'Matthew and Son' (UK #2) in 1966 at age 18.
family_context_summary: Father was a Greek Cypriot restaurateur and mother was a Swedish Baptist. They ran the Moulin Rouge restaurant on Shaftesbury Avenue in London. The family lived above the restaurant, and children helped wait tables. Parents divorced when Stevens was 8 but continued to cohabitate.
parent_family_domain_summary: Parents were restaurateurs with no music industry connections. However, the family baby grand piano provided early musical access, and Stevens' father bought him his first guitar for £8.
primary_early_advantage_tags: London 1960s pop scene, family piano, Mike Hurst mentorship, Beatles-inspired guitar, restaurant family
evidence_summary: Stevens grew up above his parents' restaurant in London's West End, with access to a baby grand piano from a young age. At 15, inspired by the Beatles, he persuaded his father to buy him a guitar for £8. He got his first publishing deal at 17 and was discovered by producer Mike Hurst (formerly of the Springfields), who helped him land a Decca/Deram record contract. His first single 'I Love My Dog' reached UK #28 and 'Matthew and Son' hit UK #2 in 1966 when he was just 18, riding the 1960s British pop music explosion. He also wrote 'The First Cut Is the Deepest' at 17, which became an enduring standard covered by multiple artists. Family had no music industry connections but the London location and cultural moment were catalytic.

name: Raúl
milestone_by_age_26: Debuted for Real Madrid's first team at age 17 in October 1994, won La Liga that season, and by age 26 had won three Champions League titles (1998, 2000, 2002), six La Liga titles, and become one of the world's greatest strikers.
early_history_summary: Raúl grew up in the San Cristóbal de los Ángeles suburb of Madrid and showed football passion from childhood. He played for San Cristóbal, then Atlético Madrid's youth academy (1990-1992), before Atlético president Jesús Gil dissolved the youth teams as too expensive. Raúl moved to Real Madrid's youth system in 1992, scored 13 goals in 7 games, and was promoted to the first team by manager Jorge Valdano in October 1994 at age 17.
primary_leverage_engine: Football instinct and elite academy pipeline
family_context_summary: Not extensively documented in reviewed sources. Raúl grew up in a working-class suburb of Madrid. His family's financial situation is not clearly documented, but the move from Atlético to Real Madrid was prompted by Atlético dissolving its youth teams for cost reasons.
parent_family_domain_summary: No evidence of family football background or professional sports connections is documented in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Real Madrid youth academy, Madrid football culture, Jorge Valdano mentorship, Atlético release catalyst, early debut
evidence_summary: Raúl grew up in a modest Madrid suburb and joined Atlético Madrid's youth academy at 13. When Atlético's president dissolved the youth teams for cost reasons, Raúl moved to Real Madrid's youth system at 15, where he scored 13 goals in 7 games and was fast-tracked to the first team by manager Jorge Valdano at age 17 in October 1994. He won La Liga in his debut season and went on to win three Champions Leagues by age 25. The Real Madrid academy provided elite facilities and pipeline, and the adversity of being released by Atlético acted as a catalyst. No family football background or financial advantage is documented.

name: Nick Drake
milestone_by_age_26: Signed to Island Records at age 20 in 1968 while still a student at Cambridge, and released three albums — 'Five Leaves Left' (1969), 'Bryter Layter' (1971), and 'Pink Moon' (1972) — all by age 24, establishing a recorded legacy that gained major posthumous acclaim.
early_history_summary: Drake was born in Rangoon, Burma to an engineer father and a musical mother who composed songs. He learned piano from an early age, attended Eagle House preparatory school and Marlborough College, then won a scholarship to Fitzwilliam College, Cambridge. While at Cambridge, he performed in London clubs and was discovered by Fairport Convention bassist Ashley Hutchings, leading to a deal with producer Joe Boyd and Island Records at age 20.
family_context_summary: Father Rodney was an engineer with the Bombay Burmah Trading Corporation. Mother Molly composed songs in the style of Noel Coward and encouraged Nick's musical education. The family lived in a country estate, Far Leys, near Tanworth-in-Arden. Drake attended boarding schools and Cambridge University.
parent_family_domain_summary: Mother Molly was a songwriter and singer whose compositions shared tonal qualities with Nick's later work. She encouraged his early piano learning and provided a reel-to-reel tape recorder for home recording. Father and grandfather attended Marlborough College, providing educational continuity.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Cambridge University, Marlborough College, musical mother, Island Records, Joe Boyd producer, British folk scene, family piano
evidence_summary: Drake benefited from a comfortable middle-class upbringing: his father was an engineer, his mother a songwriter who encouraged his musical education, and he attended elite schools (Eagle House, Marlborough College) before winning a scholarship to Cambridge. His mother's own songwriting provided a family-domain musical influence. At Cambridge, he was discovered by Fairport Convention's Ashley Hutchings and connected to producer Joe Boyd, who signed him to Island Records at age 20. His three albums were released by age 24, though they sold poorly during his lifetime. His depression and shyness created a distinctive artistic perspective but also limited his commercial trajectory. He died at age 26 in November 1974.

name: Riccardo Patrese
milestone_by_age_26: Won both the Italian and European Formula 3 championships in 1976 at age 22, after winning the Karting World Championship in 1974 at age 20, and made his Formula One debut in 1977 at age 23, scoring his first point by the end of that season.
early_history_summary: Patrese started kart racing at age 9, encouraged by his car-enthusiast father and brother. He won the Karting World Championship in 1974 at age 20, then moved to Formula Italia in 1975, Formula 3 in 1976 (winning both Italian and European championships), and Formula 2 in 1977 before making his F1 debut with Shadow at the 1977 Monaco Grand Prix at age 23. He was also a competitive skier and swimmer in his youth.
primary_leverage_engine: Karting mastery and junior formula dominance
family_context_summary: Father Mario and brother Alberto were car enthusiasts who talked about racing and racing drivers. Mother Elena was a language professor. Parents supported his racing — his father fitted out a truck to transport his Formula Italia car — but were not wealthy. Patrese described himself as 'really privileged' in family support.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father and brother were passionate about cars and motorsport, providing early immersion in racing culture. The family traveled to kart races together, with parents acting as drivers, managers, coaches, and technicians.
primary_early_advantage_tags: karting from age 9, family car culture, Italian motorsport, Scuderia Nettuno, Trivellato Chevron team, skiing/swimming athleticism
evidence_summary: Patrese started karting at age 9, supported by a car-enthusiast family that traveled to races together. He won the Karting World Championship in 1974 at age 20, which earned him a drive in Formula Italia. His father fitted out a truck to transport his car for the 1975 season. In 1976, he won both the Italian and European Formula 3 championships with Trivellato's Chevron team, and in 1977 he made his F1 debut at Monaco with Shadow. He was also a competitive skier (selected for Italian national team as a teenager) and swimmer, indicating broad athletic talent. Family was supportive but not wealthy; his father traveled with him to races.
